R-A.description: Viewpoint state and its persistence. Retiring the seeded defaults (R-IRN-1, 2, 7 to 24 and 27): `ir` means authored notation, the classic canvas v1 is unreachable, `Default Validation` is no longer seeded, `Default` becomes a system layer hidden from user surfaces while it holds no authored view, the empty viewpoint is `null` on both sides of the proxy, the VersionFixer pass 2.228 stops the seed while the purge of saved defaults is split off, and the `updateDefaultView` refresh button proves unreachable; layout per exclusive viewpoint (R-LAY-1 to 18) keeps a `layoutByViewpoint` record on `DVertex`, read through to the scalars, behind one resolver and one source of the active viewpoint. The rest is the removal of the dead `NestedView` and its cascade (R-DEAD-1 to 6), early IR authoring rows (R-A, R-B, R-B10, R-C, R-F, R-G, R-H: tabs, errors, endpoints, waypoints), channel edges hidden by `containment.edges` (R-GV-4), and two method rules: extend an existing discovery report with an addendum (R-E/E-1) and prove the search behind an assertion of absence (R-RAIL-28). 23 of 55 rows are realized, among them R-LAY-9 to 11 and 14 to 18 and the seed steps R-IRN-8 to 10, 15, 18 to 20 and 23; the layout principles R-LAY-1 to 8 and the dead-code rows except R-DEAD-5 are not.

R-B9.description: Derived viewpoints and how they are drawn. The «Derive viewpoint» dialog picks a notation (Generic by default, Petri net and its classic variant, Statechart (UML), Flowchart (ISO 5807), Activity (UML), ER (Chen) among them) and a metaclass to role table; the notations bring optional IR keys (five text and label keys, the entry mark, the arc, the end labels, the `hollowCircle` termination) under R-B9's rule that a persisted name such as a routing value never changes. Three other threads: «Color by metaclass» on the viewpoint panel (pastel swatches assigned along references, per-metaclass overrides, notation glyphs left uncoloured), the toolbar auto-layout with ELK in full (per-notation profiles, routes drawn and never persisted, outside labels reserved in its input), and seven more edge ends with conditional ends and end labels (R-EE-1 to 4). 30 of 47 rows are realized and about half are provisional; not realized are the ELK rows R-VP-40 to 48, the edge ends R-EE-1 to 4, and R-VP-52, 58, 59 and 60.

R-B9-bis.description: Three threads that meet in the IR read context and in `validateIR`, whose rules belong to authoring and never to render (R-B9-bis): IR edges (the `container` endpoint and its reactivity, object-as-edge synthesis and deletion), JjEL as the IR expression language (R-J1 to 7: a closed profile, legacy multi-hop paths migrated, `getParent` on `ReadCtx`, diagnostics always on), and the `marked` predicate (R-MK-1 to 11), read from the ephemeral run state through `ReadCtx.isMarked` and invalidated through declared dependency channels. R-IRN-4 adds the IR seed written when a view is created. Realized: R-B9-bis, R-B13 to 16 and all of R-MK; R-B17 (deleting an object-as-edge), R-IRN-4 and all of R-J are not.

R-DMV-1.description: The Data Manager and the form engine behind it, with the placement rules they replaced or refined. The Data Manager Viewpoint (R-DMV-1 to 7) is one built-in viewpoint per project whose class views without `shape` give the table columns and the drawer form, materialized at the first write; it supersedes R-VP-3 and R-VP-12 of the earlier rows R-VP-1 to 13, which place validity in the metamodel and presentation in the viewpoint, freeze the `jjodel/*` keys, set a three-rung renderer ladder (viewpoint, type, default) and limit the manager form to fields, order, sections, renderer and label. The form engine rows (R-FORM, R-WCX, R-STR) make the manager a sibling surface of the canvas over a pure engine in `jjform/` with D-graph and JSON adapters, keep the renderer precedence in the engine, record what an adapter must do (the containment cascade, deferred deletes after a write, `setName` as a primitive of its own) and let the view win in the form and, since R-STR-6 was closed, on the canvas too. 20 of 40 rows are realized; ten of the fifteen R-FORM rows, the placement criteria R-VP-1, 2 and 4 to 7, R-WCX-2 and 3, R-DMV-2 and R-DMV-7 are not.

R-EDGE-1.description: The core of the simulation engine and its configuration, with three rows on metamodel canvas edges. Engine rows: the Petri transition as the core, with fork, join, `else` and inhibitors compiled onto it, bounded weighted markings, termination distinct from deadlock and five run states; system profiles over one role catalogue, computed required roles, `simProfile` and a pure binder behind Apply; declared state attributes (stored, derived with eager evaluation and cycle checks, input), multi-valued guards and entry, exit and arc actions, with the guards and arc actions of a triggered transition reading the firing event as `event.a`, accepting places, Moore and Mealy outputs, activity final, compile defects listed at Reset, and panel lines that give the reason a guard blocks without moving the buttons. R-EDGE-1 to 3 accept a metamodel connection only between class nodes, guard the model invariant in the core setters in a separate lane, and defer any migration of saved projects. 60 of 66 rows are realized; R-EDGE-3, R-SIM-19 (state attributes declared as in an attribute grammar), R-SIM-83, 84, 85 and 93 are not.

R-GEN-1.description: Two threads joined by the oracle that checks generated code against the simulator. The code generation pilot (R-GEN-1 to 17) ships in 3.2 behind an experimental setting off by default: templates are JjEL functions with string interpolation stored as `genTemplates` in the metamodel's `_state`, every copied fragment records its origin, the one target is JavaScript run in an isolated Web Worker, and the oracle that compares it with the simulator step by step is a goal that enters 3.2 only if it is green by the freeze. The simulator's run tools (R-SIM-134 to 143 and 146) add clocks that may start with the run and belong to it, watches as invariants and breakpoints, step back, scenarios, coverage, a timeline slider and the board editor layout; R-RAIL-31, on quoting shell globs in prompts, is a stray. 24 of 29 rows are realized; R-GEN-1 (the 3.2 date), R-GEN-8 and 9 (the oracle as a goal, what stays out of the pilot), R-GEN-13 (the legacy M2T left as it is) and R-RAIL-31 are not.

R-IRN-3.description: Mostly parity between the IR object view and the native renderer (R-IRN-29 to 36): the criterion is chrome, not geometry, with `underline`, label `color` and `cornerRadius` added to the IR without migration, the separator taking the border colour, and the identity of migrated views, first matched against a moving factory and since 2026-09-24 stamped with `migratedHash`. A second theme is metaclass identity across metamodels through `authoringMetaclassPins` (R-MCID-1, 2); single rows cover a degraded custom view flagged in authoring (R-IRN-3), flat collapse fields of a graphVertex (R-IRN-37), a feature on a sibling owner judged a warning in the simulation role checks (R-SIM-89), and the renderer inspector mounted on the IR branch so its step 0 is reachable on the canvas (R-STR-7). Realized: R-IRN-29, 30, 31, 33, 35, R-MCID-1, R-SIM-89 and R-STR-7; the other six are not.

R-IRN-38.description: Editing IR labels and row values in place on the canvas, and the panel toggles that show it. One predicate decides whether a name label renames the element (R-IRN-38), a path label on an attribute of its own object edits only when the IR opts in (R-IRN-41), the value-segment toggle reads the effective `editable` value (R-IRN-40), and node and row subscriptions carry the object and metaclass names so labels follow a rename (R-IRN-39). All four rows are provisional; R-IRN-38 and R-IRN-41 are realized, R-IRN-39 and R-IRN-40 are not.

R-JS-1.description: How a JjScript run executes. A `create` is all-or-nothing on its superclasses, the dependency wait of a scope-bound M2 run accepts a one-segment name only when the bound metamodel resolves it, and Run executes in passes: forward references are deferred and retried, Run never pauses on an error, and one summary modal closes it with per-model before and after figures and the final errors. R-JS-7 (retry passes wait for every dependency) is superseded. All seven rows are realized; R-JS-2 to 6 are provisional.

R-LAY-19.description: Undo in editor-v2 under JjOM, with one layout row. R-UNDO-1 to 8 make the D-layer undo the only one, gated by `U.userHasInteracted` raised on the first pointer or key event, advance the project version only on an explicit save, keep viewpoint activation as an undo step while a selection alone is discarded and «create a view and open it» is one step, make a rename a single dispatch, and fix the copy-on-write of `CompositeActionReducer`. R-LAY-19 (several canvases of one model, each under its own viewpoint) is tied to them by R-UNDO-4, which waits on it to take the canvas viewpoint out of the D-layer. Only R-LAY-19 is realized; R-UNDO-1 to 7 are ratified and R-UNDO-8 is provisional.

R-M2U-1.description: Name uniqueness in the metamodel (M2). Names are case-sensitive and a near-homonym such as `Foo` beside `foo` is announced with a warning, not refused; classes and enumerations share one namespace across the whole metamodel, datatypes get a namespace of their own, and inherited features enter the class namespace, so shadowing is refused. The duplicate-name badge now covers M2 and the JjScript rename goes through the name setter. R-M2U-1, 2, 4 and 6 are realized; R-M2U-3 (the datatype namespace) and R-M2U-5 (the dead step 2 of `get_type`, kept and declared) are not.

R-RAIL-1.description: The properties rail and the rules learned while building it. Design rows: the rail is a shell with an inspector slot and only preset `2a`, the tree pane reuses `TreeViewContent` with a restyle, the NODE section stays in the shell behind `advanced` and closed by default, the identity block restyle moves to arc 2, the shell breadcrumb drops the metamodel segment, the shell shows abstractness as italics on the name, and tokens are consumed under fixed rules (a blacklist of 13 conflicting names, snapping to the scale, an OKLCH entity scale with one source, kept out of the tree). Method rows written along the way: conformance greps on the staged diff, the interactive `grep` as a `ugrep` wrapper, a computed style measured only on the element that paints, an order read from the data and not from a position; R-RAIL-44, the dark theme suspended, is now superseded by D-UI-15. 10 of 33 rows are realized (R-RAIL-7, 10, 14, 30, 32, 33, 34, 36, 42 and 45); the rest are not.

R-SGL-1.description: Singleton classes in M1. The singleton instance exists by construction and no path creates one (palette, canvas drop, composition menu, JjScript), switching the flag off removes every instance, the switch-on guard counts instances per model, and the «singleton» stereotype shows only on the abstract syntax. With singletons hidden, a reference to a singleton-conforming type is assigned from a select (commit B, IR branch only). R-SGL-1 to 4 and R-SGL-8 are realized; the commit plan (R-SGL-5), the six instantiation filters (R-SGL-6), the issues recorded but not closed (R-SGL-9) and the perimeter of commit B (R-SGL-10) are not.

R-SIM-1.description: Foundations of the simulation engine. The run state lives outside Redux, one per model, and the configuration sits as flat `sim*` keys in the bag of the M2 model with no core change for v1; a step interleaves with a selector instead of firing everything, and events are M1 instances with one panel button each, configured from the Trigger reference. A dozen rows build the guard and action language: the `Expression` and `Action` primitive types in the core with their migration and Ecore form, the `.[x]` state operator, strict parsing, reserved names, the evaluator hook and the marking accessor. 22 of 28 rows are realized; R-SIM-9 (initial rule per STC genre), 10 (`simSource`), 11 (`marked` as a derived view), 12 (events as M1 instances), 14 (a pure core in `model/simulation/`) and 20 (no stability before an event) are not.

R-SIM-3.description: What the user sees and touches during a simulation run. The run panel rows: the panel outside the IR, the run withdrawn when the model changes, the Simulation pill shown in Advanced mode on a metamodel whose Simulation toggle is on, a compact panel that shows state (watched attributes, marking, events) above a transport row that does not move, nondeterministic choices resolved by Ask or Random with Play, σ and `node` shown apart with nuXmv names, a navigable trace, and `node.[x]` readable by viewpoints. The I/O board (R-SIM-110 to 133) is the machine's environment, not a view: a device library (buttons, switches, sliders, keypad, clock, LEDs, displays, buzzer) bound to events, inputs and expressions over σ, saved in the M1 bag, with an editor, two skins, themes, spans, icons suggested from event names, keycaps and a floating window; most board rows are provisional. 36 of 42 rows are realized; R-SIM-92 (role outputs), 105 (the run inspector), 107 (the opt-in σ overlay), 116 and 117 (the `ioBoard` key and the binding forms) and 129 (what stays out of the first cut) are not.

R-SKIN-1.description: Form appearance presets: a closed catalogue (Slate, Paper, Ink, Mist; Slate is today's look and the default) that remaps the existing form tokens in `styles/tokens/`, orthogonal to the layout theme and with nothing the user can customise. R-SKIN-3-bis renames the vocabulary to palette (`formPalette`, `data-palette`) and moves the attribute to the `.instance-manager` root, the name persisted on the Data Manager Viewpoint singleton; R-SKIN-4 leaves the per-view skins of `irTypes.ts` untouched. All five rows are ratified and none is realized.

R-VAL-1.description: User-defined validation as a concern with its own viewpoints, separate from the syntax viewpoints, multiple and selectable, with rules activated per viewpoint and per rule. In the first slice a rule is owned by an M2 class; it is a type parallel to the view (not a `DViewElement`), accumulates with superclass rules instead of overriding them, and never blocks a write; a broken rule shows in authoring and a false one in the problems registry. Further rows cover a single reserved-name list, deleting a class that has rules, rules travelling with an imported metamodel, and no rule sign in the rail. Realized: R-VAL-1, 5, 6-bis, 7, 11 and 12; R-VAL-2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 10 are not.
